title: Egeria's diary
hookLine: a woman traveled to the Holy Land and wrote down how Jerusalem kept Holy Week

lines: READ THE STORY WHERE IT HAPPENED.
A WEEK IN JERUSALEM, WRITTEN DOWN.
cards: Dear sisters. That's who she's writing to: a circle of women back home, somewhere in the west, who can't make the trip. So she makes it for them, and writes it all down.

Her name, as it reaches us, is Egeria. She travels through the lands of the Bible, climbs mountains, asks the local monks and clergy to show her where the stories happened, and reads the passage aloud on the spot.
Then, in Jerusalem, she writes down, day by day, how the church there keeps Holy Week, the days before Easter. Because of her notebook, we can stand in that crowd.

teach.h: PALM SUNDAY: DOWN THE MOUNT OF OLIVES.
teach.b: Palm Sunday first. The people gather with their bishop on the Mount of Olives, then walk down into the city together, carrying branches of palm or olive. Children too small to walk ride on their parents' shoulders.
All the way down they sing the line the crowds sang for Jesus: "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord." They aren't just remembering the story; they're walking it, on the same hill.
That's pilgrimage: a journey to a holy place, where the walking itself becomes a prayer.

teach.h: GOOD FRIDAY: THE DEACONS STAND GUARD.
teach.b: Now Good Friday, and a startling detail. The bishop sits with the wood of the cross on a table before him, held in his hands, deacons standing around.
The people come forward one by one, bow, touch it with their forehead and eyes, and kiss it. The deacons guard it closely, she explains, because once someone bit off a piece and ran off with it.
Holiness and human nature, side by side.
The bishop preaches in Greek, but not everyone understands Greek, so a priest beside him translates into Syriac, and others explain it for those who speak Latin.
A crowd from everywhere, in one city, each hearing it in their own words.

teach.h: LET US GO INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD.
teach.b: A psalm about going up to Jerusalem begins, "I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD." Egeria went, and wrote it down so her sisters could walk where she walked, without leaving home.

how: Christians make pilgrimages to Jerusalem, Rome, Santiago de Compostela and other holy places, and some churches walk in procession with palms on Palm Sunday.

games.q: you're a deacon in Jerusalem on Good Friday. the people come one by one to kiss the wood of the cross. what's your job?
o: hand each person a splinter to take home.

practice: Bring to mind a place that mattered to you, a church, a grandmother's kitchen, a hospital corridor, a street you walked on a hard day, and go back there slowly: what you saw first, what you heard, who was there.
Then find one small detail you'd almost forgotten, the kind Egeria wrote down, and hold it as if for someone who couldn't be there.

wordCard.voice: Pilgrimage. A journey to a holy place, where the walking itself becomes a kind of prayer, and where, for Egeria, the story was read aloud on the very spot.
